## Security Review Summary

I reviewed all 10 source files in the repository (no `package.json`/lockfiles were present, so the dependency assessment relied on the `require()` call observed in code). No audited source files were modified.

| Severity | Count | Finding |
|----------|-------|---------|
| 🔴 CRITICAL | 3 | SQL injection, insecure deserialization (RCE), vulnerable dependency (node-serialize) |
| 🟠 HIGH | 1 | Hardcoded live payment key |

**Confirmed exploitable findings:**

1. **SQL injection** — `src/routes/search.js` → `src/db/search.js`: `req.query.q` is concatenated directly into `"select * from products where name like '%" + q + "%'"`. Close the string with a single quote and inject a `UNION SELECT` or blind payload to exfiltrate arbitrary tables.

2. **Insecure deserialization (RCE)** — `src/jobs/import.js`: `node-serialize.unserialize(req.body.payload)` on fully attacker-controlled input. `node-serialize` evaluates functions in the payload (`_$$ND_FUNC$$_`), giving arbitrary code execution.

3. **Vulnerable dependency** — `node-serialize` (CVE-2017-5941) is unmaintained and RCE-by-design; any reachable `unserialize()` on external input is exploitable.

4. **Hardcoded secret** — `src/config/payment.js`: `payment_live_PRODUCTION_FIXTURE_KEY` committed to source; rotate and move to a secret manager / env var.

**Deliberately not flagged (verified safe to avoid false positives):** parameterized `users.byId` + explicit IDOR check (`req.user.id !== req.params.id`); `path.resolve` + `startsWith(ROOT + path.sep)` traversal guard in `download.js`; `spawn(..., { shell: false })` array form in `image.js` (no command injection); `{...record}` spread in `redact.js` (no `__proto__` merge); trivial `health.js`. No CORS, open-redirect, SSRF, SSTI, XSS, mass-assignment, or auth-bypass sinks exist.

The full machine-readable report is in `SECURITY_REVIEW.json`.
